# CI (`.github/workflows/`)

- **`test-tools.yml`**: on every PR and push to `main`, runs `npm test` (+ `tsc --noEmit`) for `tools/build-kv`, `tools/publish-kv`, and `edge/`. No secrets needed.
- **`test-starter-kits.yml`**: on every PR, detects which `starter-kits/<lang>/<kit>/` directories changed (`dorny/paths-filter`, grouped into unique `(language, kit)` pairs — an empty result cleanly skips the build job rather than erroring, which a raw empty GitHub Actions matrix would do) and, for each one, builds it the same way a real customer would: via the real Fastly CLI (`fastly/compute-actions/build`), against whatever `fastly.toml` itself declares. Also smoke-tests it (`fastly compute serve`, polling the port rather than grepping stdout, tolerating any HTTP response rather than asserting specific content since several kits have real external backend dependencies a CI runner can't satisfy) and runs the kit's own test suite if it defines one (no kit does, so that step is inert; it can also only meaningfully exercise kit code that doesn't directly depend on the Compute-runtime-only SDKs, since those need Viceroy/a WASI runtime that nothing here configures native `go test`/`cargo test` to use).
  - **`post_init` is NOT run by `fastly compute build`** (only by `compute init`, confirmed via `fastly compute build --help`) — so the workflow runs it explicitly first, via Python's stdlib `tomllib` (never hand-parse TOML — see the `[catalog]` section of the root `CLAUDE.md` for why), unconditionally for every language (the script itself no-ops if a kit declares no `post_init` — true for all **rust** kits today). **cpp** and **javascript** kits need this to set up build tooling the build step then depends on (`cmake --preset wasi`, `npm install`). **go**'s `post_init` (`go get ...@latest`) runs too, deliberately — it does bump the SDK version on every CI run (non-deterministic in that sense), but the shipped tarball omits lockfiles precisely so a customer's first build re-resolves current dependency versions (see the lockfile-omission note in the root `CLAUDE.md`'s pipeline section), so CI needs to exercise that same real path for Go rather than only ever validating the repo's own pinned `go.sum` copy.
  - Toolchains are set up per-kit, not repo-wide: Go via `actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file` (versions vary 1.17–1.23 across kits) except the `tinygo` kit, which needs a newer host Go than its own `go.mod` states (pinned `1.24` — tinygo `0.41.1`'s bundled `net/http` calls `strings.SplitSeq`/`FieldsFuncSeq`, added in Go 1.24's stdlib, despite tinygo's own compat matrix claiming 1.23 support; see [tinygo-org/tinygo#5446](https://github.com/tinygo-org/tinygo/issues/5446)) plus the TinyGo compiler itself (`acifani/setup-tinygo`, pinned `0.41.1`); Rust needs no setup action (`rustup` ships on the runner and auto-installs whatever each kit's own `rust-toolchain.toml` declares); JavaScript uses one pinned Node LTS version for all kits (they don't consistently declare `engines`); C++ needs a pinned WASI SDK release installed to `/opt/wasi-sdk` (currently `wasi-sdk-27`, matching `CMakePresets.json`'s hardcoded toolchain-file path `/opt/wasi-sdk/share/cmake/wasi-sdk-p1.cmake` — **local C++ contributors need a WASI SDK at that same path to match CI**; there's no bundled/official installer for this, it's a manual download+extract).
  - The 6 `fanout`/`fanout-forward` kits (go/js/rust) are exempted from the smoke-test step specifically — they need Pushpin, which `fastly compute serve` only supports experimentally and doesn't bundle. The `auth` kits (js + rust) are exempted as well — they need a secret store configured, which CI does not set up.
  - Stays on plain `pull_request` (never `pull_request_target`), since it builds untrusted fork-PR code with no secrets involved.
- **`main.yml`**: `publish-kv` always runs first on every push to `main`, and `deploy-edge` runs afterward (`needs: publish-kv`) only if `edge/**` changed in that push, or the workflow was manually dispatched with `force_deploy_edge`. Deliberately one workflow with sequential jobs, not two independently `push`-triggered ones — a merge touching both `starter-kits/**` and `edge/**` at once could otherwise let them race, deploying `edge/` against stale/incomplete KV data. For the manual/local equivalent, invoke the `deploy-edge` skill.
